Deleting an entry has no confirmation.
The claim that mood syncs to analytics cannot be checked from this file.

terms.meaning: a reusable piece of the screen, written as a function that returns what to display
values the screen remembers and redraws from when they change, such as the title typed so far
the app's shared memory where notes, tasks and settings are kept
a label on each note that groups it, such as journal or general

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and client marker
sections.what: The top line marks the file to run in the browser. The imports bring in icons, the shared store, the Card, Button and Input pieces, and the mood type. Nothing shows on screen from this section alone.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page uses clicks and typing, which need to run in the browser.

sections.name: JournalView (part 1)
sections.title: State, save logic and mood options
sections.what: Holds the typed title, body and chosen mood, plus the currently selected entry. The save step ignores a blank title, adds a fixed set of journal tags, and resets the form. Also defines the four moods with their icon, label and colour.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the form values and the save rule in one place so the layout stays readable.
sections.watch_out: The starting selection is set only when the page first loads, so a newly saved entry is not highlighted automatically; the screen falls back to the first entry instead.

sections.name: JournalView (part 2)
sections.title: New entry form and mood buttons
sections.what: Shows the new entry form when toggled. It has a required title field, four mood buttons with the chosen one highlighted, a large body box, and Cancel and Save buttons. The save button label says it also syncs the mood.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user add a reflection quickly without leaving the page. The reason the mood buttons are plain buttons is not stated, but it keeps them from submitting the form.
sections.watch_out: The mood buttons must stay plain buttons; if they were submit buttons, clicking a mood would save the entry early.

sections.name: JournalView (part 3)
sections.title: Entry list and editor panel
sections.what: Lists every journal entry on the left with its date and mood label. The selected entry appears on the right with its title, time, a delete icon, and a large text area that saves each change right away.
sections.why: Likely reason: a two-column layout lets the user browse entries and read or edit one at the same time.
sections.watch_out: Edits are written to the store on every keystroke, and deleting happens at once with no undo or confirmation.

summary: The journal page where the user writes dated reflection entries, tags each one with a mood, and edits or deletes past entries.
purpose: Gives the user a place for daily reflections, with a mood recorded for each entry.
why: Likely reason: the mood choice feeds the app's analytics, as the page header says. The code in this file only saves the mood with the entry.
how: On load it selects the first journal entry. The New Reflection Entry button opens a form with a title, a mood and a body. Saving adds a note in the journal folder with fixed tags, then clears the form. The left list shows entries, and the right side shows the selected entry, where the body can be edited or the entry deleted.
inputs: Notes from the shared store, the title, mood and body typed by the user, and clicks on the list and buttons.
outputs: New or changed journal notes saved to the store, and the on-screen view of the chosen entry.
risks: Each keystroke in an entry is saved straight away. Deleting an entry has no confirmation step. The page says mood data syncs into analytics, but that happens in the store, which is not shown here.
debug: If entries do not appear, check the store's notes and whether their folder is journal. If a mood label is missing, check the mood saved on the note. If saving does nothing, check that the title is not blank, since saving stops early without one.
